evidence.source_sentence: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra of the DA-polyesters were recorded using a Perkin– Elmer system 2000 FTIR spectrometer equipped with microscope and diamond press accessories.
FTIR spectra of the as-synthesised DA-polyesters HS, HI, HT, and OT(2) are shown in Figure 1.
Due to its methyl side groups in OT(2), the asymmetric and symmetric stretching bands are observed at 2990 and 2870 cm<sup>21</sup>

while deformation bands at 1450 and $1 3 7 8 ~ \mathrm { { c m } ^ { - 1 } }$, respectively.

The characteristic stretching modes of diacetylene group $\scriptstyle - \mathrm { C } = \mathrm { C } -$C'C— are seen at about 2260 and $2 \bar { 1 } 6 0 ~ \mathrm { { c m } ^ { - 1 } }$as weak bands.

characterizations.result_summary: Tested melting temperature, melting enthalpy, exothermic reaction temperature and exothermic enthalpy of HS, HI, HT, OT(2); HS and OT(2) showed melting behavior, HT and HI had no obvious melting peak; HS and HI exhibited sharp single exothermic peak, HT and OT(2) showed broad bimodal exothermic transition; obvious exothermic peak was observed for HS at 80°C isothermal DSC, no obvious exothermic peak for aromatic DA-polyesters.

evidence.source_sentence: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) analysis was carried out employing a Perkin–Elmer DSC-7. All DA-polyesters were analyzed from 40 to 250°C under nitrogen purge at the heating rate of 10°C/min. Isothermal DSC analysis was also carried out by first heating the sample to the annealing temperature $( 8 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } )$at a rate of $3 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } / \mathrm { m i n }$.

The DSC curves of as-synthesised DA-polyesters HS, HI, HT, and OT(2) are shown in Figure 5, and the temperatures of melting $( T _ { m } )$and exothermic reaction $( T _ { \mathrm { e x o } } )$of as-synthesised DA-polyesters and their enthalpies are summarized in Table VI.
Table VI. DSC Results of the Synthesised DA-Polyesters

characterizations.result_summary: T3% (temperature at 3% weight loss) values for DA-polyesters measured in nitrogen and air indicate aromatic DA-polyesters are more thermally stable than aliphatic DA-polyester HS; degradation proceeds in two stages in air with little/no residue, and in a single stage in nitrogen with 30-40% residue.

evidence.source_sentence: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) was performed using a TA Instruments of Hi-res TGA 2950 Thermogravimetric Analyzer. A sample of about 20 mg was put into a clean platinum pan and run under both nitrogen and air atmosphere from room temperature to $8 0 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$at a heating rate of 10°C/min.

$T _ { 3 \% }$values obtained both in nitrogen and air are shown in Table V. It can be seen that aromatic DA-polyesters, HT, HI, and OT(2), are much more thermally stable than aliphatic DA-polyester HS, regardless of the testing atmosphere, due to the introduction of the benzene ring in the polymer backbone.
